answer: Committee-gated share issuance: a new identity enters only with a lotus share co-signed by 6 of 9 members drawn each epoch by beacon from the meadow of established agents. Each member signs at most three shares per epoch and locks stake behind every signature; requests travel in a walnut-sealed envelope whose blinding keeps members from recognizing colluding kin. A farm of k clones therefore needs 6k distinct signatures from rotating members, so marginal cost grows with committee breadth rather than API keys, and a share with forged lineage slashes all its signers' locks.
